propositions: Every charm has an implicit juju-info endpoint (provider, interface juju-info, global scope) supplied by Juju
A subordinate relating over juju-info gets a unit alongside each principal unit, so it rides along everywhere the principal is deployed
note: Implicit endpoint added in addCharmRelations if absent (state.go:367-374, encodeJujuInfoRelation metadata.go:468); IsImplicit at domain/deployment/charm/meta.go:240. Subordinate unit is created per principal unit entering a container-scoped relation (domain/relation/state/relation.go:1850), so strictly it rides along with every principal unit, which in the usual one-unit-per-machine layout means every machine. 'No application-specific data' is usage convention, not enforced.

propositions: A user can create a secret with a self-chosen name such as my-api-key
That name is stored as the secret's label, distinct from the URI
note: juju add-secret takes <name> as first arg (cmd/juju/secrets/add.go:61 example 'my-apitoken'); apiserver maps the name to the label and returns AlreadyExists 'secret with name' on SecretLabelAlreadyExists. No format validator on the name was found, so my-api-key is accepted. Claim begins with a stray heading fragment 'URI vs. label:)'.

propositions: Deploying or adding units without a placement directive puts each unit on a newly created machine
note: Unset placement (domain/deployment/placement.go:78) leads PlaceMachine to CreateMachine for each unit. 'Usually' is fair: --to placement can co-locate units, and subordinate units always share their principal's machine.

propositions: A subordinate's requires endpoint can have any name
Matching to the principal's implicit endpoint depends only on interface juju-info and counterpart role
note: CanRelateTo checks interface and counterpart role, never endpoint name. The 'juju-' reserved-prefix check (domain/deployment/charm/meta.go:854) is only applied to action names (actions.go:120), so naming a requires endpoint juju-info is allowed. Side effect: hasJujuInfoRelation (domain/application/state/metadata.go:505) matches by name only, so a subordinate that names its requires endpoint juju-info does not get the implicit juju-info provider endpoint added for itself.

propositions: A cross-model relation involves an offering model/application (offerer)
The consuming side is called 'saas'
correction: A cross-model relation joins an application exposed through an offer in the offering model and an application in the consuming model, where the offer appears as a SAAS entry (a remote-application proxy for the offered application).
note: In code the consumer model holds a RemoteApplicationOfferer (synthetic application representing the offered app, shown under 'SAAS' in status, cmd/juju/status/output_tabular.go:428); the offering model holds a RemoteApplicationConsumer (types.go:334). So 'saas' names the consumer-side proxy of the offered application, not the consuming side itself.

propositions: The (Vault) secret backend can be used by both machine (IAAS) and Kubernetes (CAAS) models
It is opt-in: models default to 'auto' (internal for machine, kubernetes for k8s) and must be set to the backend explicitly
note: Assumes 'It' is the Vault backend. Default model secret-backend is 'auto' (environs/config/config.go:438) resolving to internal (IAAS) or kubernetes (CAAS); the vault provider (internal/secrets/provider/vault/config.go) has no model-type restriction.

propositions: endpoint is mandatory for a Vault backend
namespace is mandatory
ca-cert is mandatory
correction: Only `endpoint` is mandatory in the Vault backend configuration; `namespace`, `ca-cert`, `token` and the other attributes are optional.
note: configSchema marks only EndpointKey Mandatory: true; namespace (line 41) and ca-cert (line 51) have no Mandatory flag; ValidateConfig only enforces client-cert/client-key pairing.

propositions: In a peer relation the 'other application' is the local application itself, so remote-application data and permissions refer to the local application
note: prepareRelationResult sets otherAppName = own application name for a single-endpoint peer relation, so the remote application seen by the charm is its own application.

propositions: A regular (non-subordinate) relation is a non-peer relation
In a regular relation both applications are principal
correction: A non-subordinate (regular) relation is a non-peer relation with global scope, which usually joins two principal applications but can also join a subordinate application through a global-scoped endpoint.
note: Relation scope is container if either endpoint is container-scoped, global otherwise; container scope requires a subordinate (relation.go:3663), but nothing forbids a subordinate in a global relation, and the subordinate watcher explicitly handles subordinate global-scoped relations (domain/relation/service/watcher.go:730).
List lead-in with no content of its own.

propositions: A Kubernetes cloud is a user-defined cloud created from an existing Kubernetes cluster's endpoint and credential
note: add-k8s: 'Creates a user-defined cloud based on a Kubernetes cluster', reading kubeconfig; Juju does not create the cluster.

propositions: Creating a secret returns its URI to the caller
A charm grants access with secret-grant using the URI, scoped to a relation
The URI can be passed as relation data
note: secret-add prints uri.String(); secret-grant takes <ID> parsed by secrets.ParseURI with required -r relation (secret-grant.go:56,76-80); add-secret CLI also prints the URI (cmd/juju/secrets/add.go). Placing the URI in relation data is convention, any string is allowed.

propositions: Either a provider or a requirer endpoint can be offered, so the offering side may be either role
note: Offer validation rejects only container-scoped endpoints; there is no role check in offer creation (GetApplicationEndpointDetails returns any role).

propositions: A relation is a connection established through endpoints
An application can take part in a relation only if it has a compatible endpoint
correction: In Juju, a relation is a connection between compatible endpoints of two applications (same interface, provider/requirer roles), or a single peer endpoint among the units of one application; an application's endpoints determine which relations it can take part in.
note: The wording conflates relation with endpoint ('a connection an application supports'). In code a relation has one (peer) or two endpoints and is created by CanRelateTo matching interface and counterpart role across different applications.
